title: Canonical coordinate Cartier realization at every root exponent
statement: Fix the finite purity setting [def-pur-conventions] and a Cartier zero section of the affine line over a $k$-scheme $T$. Use its ordinary maps [def-pur-coordinate-section-core-arrows], finite-site transport [def-pur-coordinate-section-site-arrows], root-normalized comparisons [def-pur-finite-site-coordinates], the supported pro-etale source and unit [def-amb-proetale-supported-coefficient-reduction], the constant comparison [def-amb-cartier-kummer-data], and the published Cartier arrow [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. Define cartierSource from the canonical exact closed-image single-complex comparison, the exact site/single comparison, and the specified underived supported-source comparison alpha. CartierRealization is the proposition that there exists one alpha, fixed by the supported constant unit, for which the site image of the ordinary supported Cartier arrow at every allowed annihilating exponent, followed by the canonical root-projection shifted Tate comparison, equals cartierSource followed by the single published pro-etale cartierKummerMap. The canonical zero-section coprojection and projective normalization are [def-pur-coordinate-section-coprojection-arrows], [def-pur-coordinate-section-projective-arrows].
